fields.why: A claim in the text and Discussion rests on the patients' mean tract SVI (0.63, fatal 0.73, vs 0.4 statewide), which is a continuous mean. But SVI describes the cases rather than measuring a health outcome, so leaving out continuous is also defensible.
The text states 'The majority of patients (58%) primarily lived in urban areas', so rurality belongs as a descriptor. It does not change the level.

brief_issues: Both readers give level 3 for case shares set against population shares (83% vs 12%) with comparison.scale null. The brief caps 'values only set side by side (even with framing words)' at 2 and requires a quantified contrast for level 3, yet example mm6925a1 gives level 3 for shares versus births. The brief should say whether a case share against a population share counts as a quantified shortfall.
